hints.title: Turn the absolute cosine into one variable
hints.recap: The substituted variable cannot be negative.
hints.pitfall: Replacing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>cos</mi><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></math> with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> would miss a sign branch.
hints.pause: Rearrange to a quadratic in u.

recall.reminder: An absolute value records magnitude while preserving both possible signs of the original quantity.

hints.title: Filter the algebraic roots
hints.body: Solve your quadratic. Keep only roots in the interval allowed for an absolute cosine, then recover the positive and negative cosine values associated with each permitted magnitude.
hints.recap: Intersect algebraic solutions with the range of the substituted expression.
hints.pitfall: An absolute value cannot be negative, but the underlying cosine can.
hints.pause: Find the permitted magnitudes and solve both cosine-sign branches.

recall.reminder: Intersect algebraic solutions with the range of the substituted expression.

hints.title: Count and sum within the stated interval
hints.body: Use the exact cosine values for the positive and negative magnitudes obtained from the quadratic. Retain only angles in the interval stated in the question.
hints.recap: Both the number and the sum must match the same option.
hints.pitfall: Do not add angles from a full <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>360</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> cycle.
hints.pause: Find and check the complete angle list before calculating its count and sum.

recall.reminder: Use exact angles and the supplied interval to select all trigonometric solutions.

solution:
Let u=|cosx|∈[0,1]. Then 1−2u2=u, so (2u−1)(u+1)=0. Only u=12 is allowed.

Thus cosx=±12. On 0∘≤x≤180∘, the solutions are 60∘ and 120∘. There are two solutions, with sum 180∘.

Answer A.
